expected-version.description: The version this run intends to publish, WITHOUT a leading v. Compared against the crate's actual version and the registry afterwards. Required: a default would let a caller publish whatever Cargo.toml happens to hold, which is defect 3 in a different costume.

dry-run.description: Set to "true" to run cargo publish --dry-run and publish nothing.

steps.name: Refuse a rehearsal, a prerelease, or the wrong version
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail

# cargo metadata, not a grep of Cargo.toml: the published version is
# what cargo resolves, and that is the only number that matters here.
ACTUAL="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 \
  | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.name == "quipu-ai") | .version')"

# The refusals live in a script so they can be OBSERVED rather than
# asserted: scripts/ci/crates-publish-guard.sh --selftest proves all of
# them, plus a control arm, without cutting a release. A safety property
# that has only ever been reasoned about is a claim.
bash scripts/ci/crates-publish-guard.sh "$EXPECTED" "$ACTUAL" "$REF_NAME"

steps.name: Record what crates.io serves now
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
# crates.io REQUIRES a User-Agent. Without one it answers 403, which
# reads as "blocked" or "absent" and sent the first pass of aegis-pb4rzi
# down the wrong path entirely. A 403 from a public read is usually a
# missing header, not a permission.
BEFORE="$(curl -sS --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 \
  -H 'User-Agent: quipu-release-ci (github.com/scbrown/quipu)' \
  https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/quipu-ai \
  | jq -r '.crate.max_version // "none"')"
echo "before=${BEFORE}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
echo "crates.io currently serves: ${BEFORE}"

# ALREADY-PUBLISHED IS A SUCCESS, NOT A FAILURE. This action runs after
# the asset jobs, so it will be re-run whenever one of those is re-run,
# and `cargo publish` on an existing version exits non-zero. A lane that
# cannot be re-run is a lane people work around by hand, which is how
# publishing stops being automatic in the first place.
#
# Skipping the publish is safe here precisely because the version was
# asserted equal to the caller's intent in the step above: this can only
# mean "the version we meant to ship is the version being served".
if [ "$BEFORE" = "${{ inputs.expected-version }}" ]; then
  echo "already=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  echo "::notice::crates.io already serves ${BEFORE} — nothing to publish."
else
  echo "already=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
fi

steps.name: Publish (dry run)
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
cargo publish --dry-run
# Say it in the log, because the job's CONCLUSION cannot. A dry run and
# a real publish both end in `success`, and that indistinguishability is
# defect 2 above.
echo "::notice::DRY RUN — nothing was published. crates.io still serves" \
     "${{ steps.before.outputs.before }}, not ${EXPECTED}."

steps.name: Verify crates.io actually moved
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
for attempt in $(seq 1 10); do
  NOW="$(curl -sS --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 \
    -H 'User-Agent: quipu-release-ci (github.com/scbrown/quipu)' \
    https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/quipu-ai \
    | jq -r '.crate.max_version // "none"')"
  echo "attempt ${attempt}: crates.io serves ${NOW} (want ${EXPECTED})"
  if [ "$NOW" = "$EXPECTED" ]; then
    echo "::notice::crates.io moved ${BEFORE} -> ${NOW}"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 15
done
echo "::error::cargo publish succeeded but crates.io still serves ${NOW}," \
     "not ${EXPECTED}. The publish did not take effect — do NOT read this" \
     "lane's earlier green steps as evidence that it did (aegis-pb4rzi)."
exit 1
